claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Liochev et al., 1999, Paterson et al., 2002, and Copp et al., 2017.

claims.claim: NfsA is thought to guard against oxidative stress through reduction of water-soluble quinones such as 1,4-benzoquinone.
claims.source: Expression of nfsA is governed by the soxRS regulon, and NfsA is thought to guard against oxidative stress through reduction of water-soluble quinones such as 1,4-benzoquinone (Liochev et al., 1999; Paterson et al., 2002; Copp et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Liochev et al., 1999, Paterson et al., 2002, and Copp et al., 2017.

claims.claim: NfsA is able to reduce a wide diversity of nitroaromatic compounds.
claims.source: Although most efficient with quinone substrates, NfsA is also able to reduce a wide diversity of nitroaromatic compounds (Valiauga et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Valiauga et al., 2017.

claims.claim: There are relatively few nitroaromatic natural products.
claims.source: This is generally believed to represent non-physiological substrate ambiguity, as there are relatively few nitroaromatic natural products, and in many cases nitro-reduction yields a more toxic derivative (Winkler and Hertweck, 2007; Parry et al., 2011; Williams et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Winkler and Hertweck, 2007, Parry et al., 2011, and Williams et al., 2015.

claims.claim: In many cases nitro-reduction yields a more toxic derivative.
claims.source: This is generally believed to represent non-physiological substrate ambiguity, as there are relatively few nitroaromatic natural products, and in many cases nitro-reduction yields a more toxic derivative (Winkler and Hertweck, 2007; Parry et al., 2011; Williams et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Winkler and Hertweck, 2007, Parry et al., 2011, and Williams et al., 2015.

claims.claim: Nitro-reduction of chloramphenicol transforms this antibiotic to a product that is not discernibly toxic to bacteria.
claims.source: An important exception is that nitro-reduction of chloramphenicol transforms this antibiotic to a product that is not discernibly toxic to bacteria (Yunis, 1988; Erwin et al., 2007; Crofts et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Yunis, 1988, Erwin et al., 2007, and Crofts et al., 2019.

claims.claim: Over-expressed native NfsA confers only slight chloramphenicol protection to E. coli host cells.
claims.source: We have observed that over-expressed native NfsA confers only slight chloramphenicol protection to E. coli host cells, but reasoned that we could select for improved detoxification in an extremely high-throughput manner by plating variant libraries on chloramphenicol-amended media.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on the authors' own observations.

claims.claim: Members of the bacterial nitroreductase superfamily appear to have unusually plastic active sites.
claims.source: Because members of the bacterial nitroreductase superfamily appear to have unusually plastic active sites (Akiva et al., 2017), we considered that simultaneous mass-mutagenesis of up to eight active-site residues should be possible.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Akiva et al., 2017.

claims.claim: The degenerate gene library represented 430 million possible gene combinations, collectively specifying 394 million different NfsA variants.
claims.source: In total, our library represented 430 million possible gene combinations, collectively specifying 394 million different NfsA variants.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on the design of the degenerate gene library described in the manuscript.

claims.claim: A total of 398 million transformed colonies were recovered, representing 252 million different NfsA variants.
claims.source: We ultimately recovered a total of 398 million transformed colonies, a collection predicted by GLUE (Firth and Patrick, 2008) to represent 252 million different NfsA variants.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data and computational prediction using GLUE.

claims.claim: Approximately 0.05% of the gene variants (~200,000 clones) were more effective than wild-type nfsA at enabling colony formation on LB agar amended with 3 µM chloramphenicol.
claims.source: Despite the drastic reconfiguration of their encoded active sites, a surprising 0.05% of the gene variants (~200,000 clones) were more effective than wild-type nfsA (i.e. enabled colony formation on LB agar amended with 3 µM chloramphenicol, the lowest concentration at which wild-type nfsA was unable to support host cell growth).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental selection data.

claims.claim: 30 top variants exhibited evidence of a conserved genetic response to the chloramphenicol selection.
claims.source: Sequencing and elimination of duplicates yielded 30 top variants that exhibited evidence of a conserved genetic response to the chloramphenicol selection.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on sequencing data of selected variants.

claims.claim: In the top 30 variants, the native serine or threonine at positions 41 and 219 was substituted by an aromatic residue in ≥26 of the 30 cases.
claims.source: Particularly strong trends were observed at positions 41 and 219 (where the native serine or threonine was substituted by an aromatic residue in ≥26 of the 30 cases), and at position 225 (100% substitution of the native arginine by an uncharged or acidic residue) (Figure 1C, Supplementary file 1a).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on sequencing data of the top 30 variants and is shown in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: At position 225, 100% of the top 30 variants had substitution of the native arginine by an uncharged or acidic residue.
claims.source: Particularly strong trends were observed at positions 41 and 219 (where the native serine or threonine was substituted by an aromatic residue in ≥26 of the 30 cases), and at position 225 (100% substitution of the native arginine by an uncharged or acidic residue) (Figure 1C, Supplementary file 1a).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on sequencing data of the top 30 variants and is shown in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: 7NT cells expressing the 30 top variants demonstrated nearly 6- to 10-fold greater chloramphenicol tolerance than those expressing native nfsA.
claims.source: In EC50 assays, 7NT cells expressing these 30 variants demonstrated nearly 6- to 10-fold greater chloramphenicol tolerance than those expressing native nfsA (Figure 1D).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on EC50 assay data shown in Figure 1D.

claims.claim: There was no substantial variation in expression between the top 30 variants and native nfsA.
claims.source: SDS-PAGE analysis revealed that there was no substantial variation in expression between these variants and native nfsA, and hence the enhanced chloramphenicol detoxification was not a consequence of elevated expression levels (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on SDS-PAGE analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The enhanced chloramphenicol detoxification was not a consequence of elevated expression levels.
claims.source: SDS-PAGE analysis revealed that there was no substantial variation in expression between these variants and native nfsA, and hence the enhanced chloramphenicol detoxification was not a consequence of elevated expression levels (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from SDS-PAGE data showing similar expression levels.

claims.claim: The top five chloramphenicol-detoxifying NfsA variants exhibited only marginal (at most 2.2-fold) improvements in chloramphenicol kcat/KM over wild-type NfsA.
claims.source: We were surprised to discover that these variants exhibited only marginal (at most 2.2-fold) improvements in chloramphenicol kcat/KM over wild-type NfsA (Table 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on steady-state kinetics assay data shown in Table 1.

claims.claim: The top five variants were impaired in kcat (6–10-fold lower than NfsA) but greatly improved in KM (8–13-fold lower than NfsA).
claims.source: However, in every case the variants were impaired in kcat (6–10-fold lower than NfsA) but greatly improved in KM (8–13-fold lower than NfsA).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on kinetic parameters measured in steady-state kinetics assays.

claims.claim: The in vivo improvements in chloramphenicol detoxification were driven primarily by enhanced substrate affinity.
claims.source: Thus, it appeared that the in vivo improvements in chloramphenicol detoxification were driven primarily by enhanced substrate affinity.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the kinetic data showing improved KM but decreased kcat.

claims.claim: 1,4-benzoquinone reduction was unmeasurable in each of the five top chloramphenicol-detoxifying variants.
claims.source: However, when assayed individually we found that 1,4-benzoquinone reduction was unmeasurable in each of the five top chloramphenicol-detoxifying variants (Table 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on enzyme activity assay data shown in Table 1.

claims.claim: For wild-type NfsA, 1,4-benzoquinone reduction (kcat/KM = 5.8 × 10^6) is nearly 1000-fold more efficient than chloramphenicol reduction.
claims.source: In contrast, for wild-type NfsA, 1,4-benzoquinone reduction (kcat/KM = 5.8 × 106; Valiauga et al., 2017) is nearly 1000-fold more efficient than chloramphenicol reduction (Table 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on kinetic data from Table 1 and a citation to Valiauga et al., 2017.

claims.claim: The data are consistent with in vivo chloramphenicol reduction having been amplified for the selected variants by the elimination of competitive quinone inhibition.
claims.source: Our data are therefore consistent with in vivo chloramphenicol reduction having been amplified for the selected variants by the elimination of competitive quinone inhibition.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the kinetic data showing loss of quinone activity and improved chloramphenicol activity.

claims.claim: Variant 36_37 has seven substitutions: S41Y, H215C, T219Y, K222V, S224R, R225V, F227G.
claims.source: The top two chloramphenicol-detoxifying variants (on the basis of EC50 measurements; 36_37 and 20_39) each had seven substitutions at the eight targeted positions, with both containing the wild-type residue leucine at position 43 (36_37 = S41Y, H215C, T219Y, K222V, S224R, R225V, F227G; 20_39 = S41Y, H215N, T219Y, K222R, S224Y, R225D, F227H; Figure 2A–C).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on sequencing data and structural models shown in Figure 2A-C.

claims.claim: Variant 20_39 has seven substitutions: S41Y, H215N, T219Y, K222R, S224Y, R225D, F227H.
claims.source: The top two chloramphenicol-detoxifying variants (on the basis of EC50 measurements; 36_37 and 20_39) each had seven substitutions at the eight targeted positions, with both containing the wild-type residue leucine at position 43 (36_37 = S41Y, H215C, T219Y, K222V, S224R, R225V, F227G; 20_39 = S41Y, H215N, T219Y, K222R, S224Y, R225D, F227H; Figure 2A–C).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on sequencing data and structural models shown in Figure 2A-C.

claims.claim: There are 126 possible intermediate forms between wild-type NfsA and each selected variant.
claims.source: Therefore, there are 126 possible intermediate forms (27 – 2) between wild-type NfsA and each selected variant.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on mathematical calculation of possible combinations.

claims.claim: There was no clear path from NfsA to either variant 36_37 or 20_39 that involved exclusively upward steps in the hypothetical evolutionary trajectory.
claims.source: In neither case was there a clear path from NfsA to the final variant that involved exclusively upward steps in the hypothetical evolutionary trajectory (Figure 2D–F).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on analysis of all intermediate variants shown in Figure 2D-F.

claims.claim: The final two substitutions (H215C and K222V for variant 36_37, and K222R and S224Y for variant 20_39) did not contribute substantially to the overall chloramphenicol-detoxifying activity of each variant.
claims.source: Nevertheless, it was evident that the final two substitutions (H215C and K222V for variant 36_37, and K222R and S224Y for variant 20_39) did not contribute substantially to the overall chloramphenicol-detoxifying activity of each variant.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on analysis of intermediate variant activities.

claims.claim: Iterative evolutionary strategies could have plausibly generated NfsA variants exhibiting similar levels of chloramphenicol-detoxifying activity to 36_37 and 20_39, but there were very few accessible pathways for this.
claims.source: Thus, we concluded that iterative evolutionary strategies could have plausibly generated NfsA variants exhibiting similar levels of chloramphenicol-detoxifying activity to 36_37 and 20_39, but that there were very few accessible pathways for this (Figure 2D–E).
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the evolutionary trajectory analysis shown in Figure 2D-E.

claims.claim: Only one of the seven substitutions present in each of variants 36_37 and 20_39 significantly enhanced chloramphenicol detoxification when introduced on an individual basis.
claims.source: Most prominently, we noted that only one of the seven substitutions present in each of variants 36_37 and 20_39 significantly enhanced chloramphenicol detoxification when introduced on an individual basis (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: The single substitution that significantly enhanced chloramphenicol detoxification was at residue R225 in both variants.
claims.source: Although it was the same residue, R225, that was substituted in each case, the substituting residues possessed very different chemical properties (negatively charged aspartate in 20_39 versus non-polar valine in 36_37).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data and analysis of individual substitutions.

claims.claim: None of the top 30 selected variants had retained an arginine at position 225.
claims.source: This, together with the observation that none of our top 30 selected variants had retained an arginine at position 225 (Figure 1C, Supplementary file 1a), suggested that it was important for arginine 225 to be eliminated before the other active-site substitutions could make a discernible contribution to improved chloramphenicol detoxification.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on sequencing data shown in Figure 1C and Supplementary file 1a.

claims.claim: It was important for arginine 225 to be eliminated before the other active-site substitutions could make a discernible contribution to improved chloramphenicol detoxification.
claims.source: This, together with the observation that none of our top 30 selected variants had retained an arginine at position 225 (Figure 1C, Supplementary file 1a), suggested that it was important for arginine 225 to be eliminated before the other active-site substitutions could make a discernible contribution to improved chloramphenicol detoxification.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that all top variants lack R225 and individual substitution data.

claims.claim: S41Y and T219Y did not confer a significant improvement in chloramphenicol detoxification when introduced to NfsA individually or together.
claims.source: For example, both of the top selected variants contained the substitutions S41Y and T219Y, neither of which conferred a significant improvement in chloramphenicol detoxification when introduced to NfsA individually (Figure 3A) or together (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3A and 3B.

claims.claim: When S41Y was introduced into an R225V or R225D background, it yielded a significant increase in chloramphenicol detoxification.
claims.source: When each was introduced into an R225V or R225D background, S41Y yielded a significant increase in chloramphenicol detoxification, but T219Y did not (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: The combination of S41Y and T219Y together with R225V or R225D gave a further significant improvement in chloramphenicol detoxification.
claims.source: However, the combination of S41Y and T219Y together with R225V or R225D gave a further significant improvement (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Complex epistatic interactions render >99% of the 5040 hypothetical evolutionary pathways broadly inaccessible to iterative mutagenesis strategies.
claims.source: Overall, our data suggest that complex epistatic interactions render >99% of the 5040 hypothetical evolutionary pathways (that might be traversed from wild-type NfsA to either 36_37 or 20_39) broadly inaccessible to iterative mutagenesis strategies.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the analysis of all evolutionary trajectories and epistatic interactions.

claims.claim: The first substitution of both hypothetical trajectories (i.e. the elimination of R225) was sufficient to abolish nearly all 1,4-benzoquinone activity.
claims.source: From these data, it was evident that the first substitution of both hypothetical trajectories (i.e. the elimination of R225) was sufficient to abolish nearly all 1,4-benzoquinone activity.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on kinetic assay data of intermediate variants.

claims.claim: R225 plays a key role in binding 1,4-benzoquinone substrate.
claims.source: A structure of NfsA with 1,4-benzoquinone in the active site was reported from the Hyde group that proposes the quinone is held in place through interactions between one of its carbonyl oxygens and the backbone of S41, while the other carbonyl oxygen interacts with the guanidinium of R225 and/or the amine of Q67 (Day, 2013). Our data are consistent with R225 playing a key role in binding this substrate.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Day, 2013 and is consistent with the authors' experimental data.

claims.claim: The level of 1,4-benzoquinone activity remained unmeasurably low with all subsequent substitutions after R225 elimination.
claims.source: The level of 1,4-benzoquinone activity remained unmeasurably low with all subsequent substitutions (Figure 4A and B).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on kinetic assay data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claims.claim: The sustained loss of 1,4-benzoquinone activity throughout each trajectory is consistent with elimination of quinone competition promoting more effective chloramphenicol reduction.
claims.source: The sustained loss of 1,4-benzoquinone activity throughout each trajectory is consistent with elimination of quinone competition promoting more effective chloramphenicol reduction.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the kinetic data showing loss of quinone activity and improved chloramphenicol activity.

claims.claim: Variants that retained R225 were on average no better than wild-type NfsA at defending host cells against chloramphenicol (mean fold improvement of 1.0 ± 0.5).
claims.source: The variants that retained R225 were on average no better than wild-type NfsA at defending host cells against chloramphenicol (mean fold improvement of 1.0 ± 0.5), while cells expressing variants that contained the substitution R225V or R225D were on average able to tolerate 4.0 ± 2.4 fold higher chloramphenicol concentrations than those expressing wild-type nfsA (Supplementary file 1c).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on analysis of all intermediate variants shown in Supplementary file 1c.

claims.claim: Cells expressing variants that contained the substitution R225V or R225D were on average able to tolerate 4.0 ± 2.4 fold higher chloramphenicol concentrations than those expressing wild-type nfsA.
claims.source: The variants that retained R225 were on average no better than wild-type NfsA at defending host cells against chloramphenicol (mean fold improvement of 1.0 ± 0.5), while cells expressing variants that contained the substitution R225V or R225D were on average able to tolerate 4.0 ± 2.4 fold higher chloramphenicol concentrations than those expressing wild-type nfsA (Supplementary file 1c).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on analysis of all intermediate variants shown in Supplementary file 1c.

claims.claim: The substitution S41Y yielded a profound improvement in chloramphenicol KM, but also diminished kcat substantially.
claims.source: The substitution S41Y that came next in both trajectories yielded a profound improvement in chloramphenicol KM, but also diminished kcat substantially (Figure 4B and C and Figure 4F and G).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on kinetic data shown in Figure 4B, C, F, and G.

claims.claim: S41Y most likely enables planar stabilisation and stacking of nitroaromatic substrates between the isoalloxazine rings of flavin mononucleotide (FMN) and the introduced tyrosine.
claims.source: We observed the same S41Y NfsA substitution in our previous PR-104A study, and concluded that this most likely enables planar stabilisation and stacking of nitroaromatic substrates between the isoalloxazine rings of flavin mononucleotide (FMN) and the introduced tyrosine (Copp et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on a previous study by the authors (Copp et al., 2017) and inference from structural considerations.

claims.claim: The improved affinity for chloramphenicol is likely explained by planar stabilisation and stacking between FMN and the introduced tyrosine, with the decrease in catalytic turnover arising as a consequence of enhanced stabilisation of the Michaelis complex.
claims.source: It is likely that a similar phenomenon explains the improved affinity for chloramphenicol observed here, with the decrease in catalytic turnover also arising as a consequence of enhanced stabilisation of the Michaelis complex.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from kinetic data and structural considerations.

claims.claim: The subsequent substitutions after S41Y act to 'tune' the system, exerting only minor effects on kcat, but overall yielding incremental improvements in chloramphenicol KM.
claims.source: The subsequent substitutions in each trajectory then act to 'tune' the system, exerting only minor effects on kcat, but overall yielding incremental improvements in chloramphenicol KM that largely mirror the improved chloramphenicol detoxification observed in vivo (Figure 4C and E and Figure 4D and F).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on kinetic data shown in Figure 4C, D, E, and F.

claims.claim: The expression levels were consistent for each intermediate variant throughout the hypothetical evolutionary progression.
claims.source: SDS-PAGE analysis confirmed that the expression levels were consistent for each intermediate variant throughout the hypothetical evolutionary progression, eliminating this as a variable exerting substantial influence on the relative activity levels in vivo (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on SDS-PAGE analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Using epPCR to introduce mutations across the entire nfsA coding sequence, 50 unique sequences were identified, each of which encoded a protein that was substituted at the R225 position.
claims.source: When each gene variant was sequenced, it was revealed that there were 50 unique sequences, each of which encoded a protein that was substituted at the R225 position (Supplementary file 1e).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on sequencing data of epPCR-selected variants shown in Supplementary file 1e.

claims.claim: Sequencing of 20 randomly-chosen clones grown without chloramphenicol selection identified no R225 substitutions, confirming that the epPCR library was not profoundly biased towards mutation of codon 225.
claims.source: In contrast, sequencing of 20 randomly-chosen clones grown without chloramphenicol selection identified no R225 substitutions, confirming that the epPCR library was not profoundly biased towards mutation of codon 225 (Supplementary file 1f).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on sequencing data of unselected clones shown in Supplementary file 1f.

claims.claim: Codon 225 was mutated exclusively at the first nucleotide position, giving substitutions R225C (C→T, 47 times), R225S (C→A, seven times) or R225G (C→G, six times).
claims.source: We were surprised to note (Supplementary file 1e) that codon 225 was mutated exclusively at the first nucleotide position, giving substitutions R225C (C→T, 47 times), R225S (C→A, seven times) or R225G (C→G, six times), but not at the second nucleotide position (which would have given rise to R225L/P/H).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on sequencing data shown in Supplementary file 1e.

claims.claim: 100% of epPCR-selected variants were mutated at codon 225.
claims.source: Irrespective, that 100% of selected variants were mutated at codon 225 provides compelling evidence that eliminating quinone competition is a key first step towards evolving improved chloramphenicol detoxification, and that substitution of R225 is the most attainable way to achieve this.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on sequencing data of epPCR-selected variants.

claims.claim: Eliminating quinone competition is a key first step towards evolving improved chloramphenicol detoxification.
claims.source: Irrespective, that 100% of selected variants were mutated at codon 225 provides compelling evidence that eliminating quinone competition is a key first step towards evolving improved chloramphenicol detoxification, and that substitution of R225 is the most attainable way to achieve this.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that all selected variants have R225 substitutions and the loss of quinone activity.

claims.claim: Substitution of R225 is the most attainable way to eliminate quinone competition.
claims.source: Irrespective, that 100% of selected variants were mutated at codon 225 provides compelling evidence that eliminating quinone competition is a key first step towards evolving improved chloramphenicol detoxification, and that substitution of R225 is the most attainable way to achieve this.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that all selected variants have R225 substitutions.

claims.claim: For four of the five prodrugs tested, host sensitivity was largely unchanged (EC50 within a range of 0.8 to 2-fold that of the NfsA-expressing strain) when expressing any of the variants.
claims.source: However, for four of the five prodrugs, host sensitivity was largely unchanged (EC50 within a range of 0.8 to 2-fold that of the NfsA-expressing strain) when expressing any of the variants (Figure 5C–F).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on EC50 assay data shown in Figure 5C-F.

claims.claim: All variants exhibited similar gains in metronidazole activity to chloramphenicol, despite the two compounds sharing little structural similarity.
claims.source: The exception was metronidazole, for which all variants exhibited similar gains in activity to chloramphenicol, despite the two compounds sharing little structural similarity (Figure 5A–B).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on EC50 assay data shown in Figure 5A-B.

claims.claim: The introduction of R225V or R225D substitutions into NfsA significantly enhanced activity with metronidazole and CB1954.
claims.source: Moreover, the introduction of R225V or R225D substitutions into NfsA (which largely eliminate 1,4-benzoquinone activity; Figure 4A–B) did not improve reduction of all prodrugs, but only significantly enhanced activity with metronidazole and CB1954 (Student's t-test; Figure 5B,D).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on EC50 assay data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 5B and D.

claims.claim: Selection for enhanced chloramphenicol detoxification was not driven exclusively by loss of the competing quinone activity.
claims.source: We therefore concluded that our selection for enhanced chloramphenicol detoxification was not driven exclusively by loss of the competing quinone activity, as this would have tended to also enhance activity with other alternate substrates.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that not all prodrug activities were enhanced.

claims.claim: Metronidazole is cheap, widely-available, and has no measurable bystander effect in E. coli.
claims.source: Because metronidazole is cheap, widely-available, and has no measurable bystander effect in E. coli (i.e. unlike many other nitroaromatic prodrugs its toxic metabolites are confined solely to the activating cell [Chan-Hyams et al., 2018]), we considered it ideally suited for counter-selection applications.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Chan-Hyams et al., 2018.

claims.claim: Chloramphenicol maintained plasmids bearing either 36_37 or 20_39 in E. coli 7NT in 100% of cases (94/94 colonies tested).
claims.source: The resulting colonies were then tested for retention or loss of the plasmid, respectively, with the expected outcome being realised in 100% of cases (94/94 colonies tested; Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Metronidazole forced elimination of plasmids bearing either 36_37 or 20_39 in E. coli 7NT in 100% of cases (94/94 colonies tested).
claims.source: The resulting colonies were then tested for retention or loss of the plasmid, respectively, with the expected outcome being realised in 100% of cases (94/94 colonies tested; Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The selected variants might have useful applications as dual selectable/counter-selectable marker genes.
claims.source: This suggests that our selected variants might indeed have useful applications as dual selectable/counter-selectable marker genes.
claims.evidence: The claim is speculative, based on the observed selection and counter-selection properties.

claims.claim: The reconstructed NfsA 'engine' is unlikely to be an optimal fit within the pre-existing chassis.
claims.source: We acknowledge that this approach of focusing exclusively on eight key active-site residues means the reconstructed NfsA 'engine' is unlikely to be an optimal fit within the pre-existing chassis, and that further gains in activity would undoubtedly result by selecting residue substitutions in the second shell, or beyond.
claims.evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning by the authors about the limitations of their approach.

claims.claim: Further gains in activity would undoubtedly result by selecting residue substitutions in the second shell, or beyond.
claims.source: We acknowledge that this approach of focusing exclusively on eight key active-site residues means the reconstructed NfsA 'engine' is unlikely to be an optimal fit within the pre-existing chassis, and that further gains in activity would undoubtedly result by selecting residue substitutions in the second shell, or beyond.
claims.evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning by the authors about potential improvements.

claims.claim: Error-prone PCR can only access a limited and unbalanced repertoire of residues (on average, only 5.7 of the 19 alternative amino acids per codon position, with a bias towards similar residues).
claims.source: Nevertheless, we reasoned that our approach would allow us to gain comprehensive insight into key catalytic changes driving improved chloramphenicol detoxification, without being subject to the stochastic vagaries of epPCR, or the well-established phenomenon that it can only access a limited and unbalanced repertoire of residues (on average, only 5.7 of the 19 alternative amino acids per codon position, with a bias towards similar residues [Hermes et al., 1990]).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hermes et al., 1990.

claims.claim: The strong trade-off between quinone and chloramphenicol reduction is a very different scenario to the predominantly weak trade-offs observed in previous laboratory evolution studies.
claims.source: The strong trade-off between quinone and chloramphenicol reduction is a very different scenario to the predominantly weak trade-offs observed in previous laboratory evolution studies (e.g. those reviewed by Kaltenbach et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: The claim compares the current findings to previous studies reviewed by Kaltenbach et al., 2016.

claims.claim: Ben-David et al., 2020 encountered an abrupt activity trade-off when they evolved the calcium-dependent lactonase mammalian paraoxonase-1 into an efficient organophosphate hydrolase.
claims.source: Even the more recent work of Ben-David et al., 2020 who encountered an abrupt activity trade-off when they evolved the calcium-dependent lactonase mammalian paraoxonase-1 into an efficient organophosphate hydrolase, found that the native functionality could subsequently be restored and was not incompatible with the evolved one (Ben-David et al., 2013; Ben-David et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Ben-David et al., 2013 and Ben-David et al., 2020.

claims.claim: In the Ben-David et al. study, the native functionality could subsequently be restored and was not incompatible with the evolved one.
claims.source: Even the more recent work of Ben-David et al., 2020 who encountered an abrupt activity trade-off when they evolved the calcium-dependent lactonase mammalian paraoxonase-1 into an efficient organophosphate hydrolase, found that the native functionality could subsequently be restored and was not incompatible with the evolved one (Ben-David et al., 2013; Ben-David et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Ben-David et al., 2013 and Ben-David et al., 2020.

claims.claim: Most previous laboratory evolution studies have evaded the phenomenon of active selection against the original function by focusing on heterologous enzymes and/or exogenously applied substrates.

results.result: NfsA is a promiscuous FMN-dependent oxidoreductase from E. coli that primarily reduces quinones for oxidative stress protection but can also reduce diverse nitroaromatic compounds including chloramphenicol. The enzyme belongs to a superfamily with unusually plastic active sites and diverse functionalities.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C7, C9, C77, C82-C86 establish the background context for NfsA through citations to prior literature. These claims describe well-established properties of NfsA and the nitroreductase superfamily, supported by appropriate references to published work.

results.result: A degenerate gene library representing 430 million possible gene combinations (394 million unique NfsA variants) was constructed. Following transformation, 398 million colonies were recovered representing 252 million unique variants, with approximately 0.05% (~200,000 clones) showing improved chloramphenicol resistance compared to wild-type.
results.evaluation: Claims C10-C12 describe the library construction and selection results with specific quantitative data. The library size calculations are mathematically sound based on the degenerate codon design (C10), recovery numbers are experimentally determined (C11), and the selection outcome is clearly measured (C12).

results.result: Sequencing of 30 top chloramphenicol-resistant variants revealed strong selection for aromatic residues at positions 41 and 219 (≥26/30 cases) and 100% substitution of R225 with uncharged or acidic residues. These variants conferred 6-10-fold improved chloramphenicol tolerance without changes in expression levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C13-C18 present sequencing and phenotypic data for selected variants. The genetic trends (C14-C15) are clearly documented in Figure 1C and Supplementary file 1a, EC50 improvements (C16) are shown in Figure 1D, and expression analysis (C17-C18) in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 confirms similar protein levels.

results.result: The top five chloramphenicol-detoxifying variants showed only marginal improvements in kcat/KM (≤2.2-fold) due to decreased kcat (6-10-fold) but greatly improved KM (8-13-fold). These variants completely lost 1,4-benzoquinone activity, suggesting improved in vivo chloramphenicol detoxification resulted from enhanced substrate affinity and elimination of competitive quinone inhibition.
results.evaluation: Claims C19-C24 present kinetic data from Table 1 showing the trade-off between kcat and KM (C19-C20), leading to the inference about substrate affinity driving in vivo improvements (C21). The complete loss of quinone activity (C22-C23) and the mechanistic interpretation (C24) are well-supported by the data, though C24 is an inference rather than direct measurement.

results.result: The two top variants (36_37 and 20_39) each contained seven substitutions with 126 possible intermediates between wild-type and each variant. Analysis of all intermediates revealed no clear exclusively upward evolutionary path, though iterative strategies could plausibly have generated similar variants with very few accessible pathways.
results.evaluation: Claims C25-C30 describe the evolutionary trajectory analysis. The variant sequences (C25-C26) are experimentally determined, the number of intermediates (C27) is mathematically correct, and the trajectory analysis (C28-C30) is based on comprehensive experimental testing of all 126 intermediates for each variant as shown in Figure 2D-F.

results.result: Only R225 substitution significantly enhanced chloramphenicol detoxification when introduced individually, with 100% of top 30 variants lacking arginine at position 225. Other substitutions like S41Y and T219Y showed epistatic interactions, requiring R225 elimination before contributing to improved activity. Complex epistasis rendered >99% of 5040 hypothetical evolutionary pathways inaccessible to iterative mutagenesis.
results.evaluation: Claims C31-C38 demonstrate extensive epistasis through systematic testing of individual and combined substitutions. The data in Figure 3A-B clearly show that only R225 substitution improves activity alone (C31-C32), all top variants lack R225 (C33), and epistatic interactions are evident (C35-C37). The conclusion about pathway accessibility (C38) is a reasonable inference from the comprehensive intermediate analysis.

results.result: R225 elimination abolished nearly all 1,4-benzoquinone activity in both evolutionary trajectories, with activity remaining unmeasurable through all subsequent substitutions. Variants retaining R225 showed no improvement in chloramphenicol resistance (1.0±0.5-fold), while R225V/D variants conferred 4.0±2.4-fold improved tolerance, consistent with elimination of quinone competition promoting chloramphenicol reduction.
results.evaluation: Claims C39-C44 present kinetic data for intermediate variants showing loss of quinone activity (C39, C41) supported by Figure 4A-B and Supplementary file 1b. The structural interpretation (C40) is supported by citation to Day, 2013 and consistent with the data. The statistical comparison of R225-containing vs R225-substituted variants (C43-C44) from Supplementary file 1c strongly supports the mechanistic interpretation (C42).

results.result: The S41Y substitution profoundly improved chloramphenicol KM but decreased kcat, likely through planar stabilization between FMN and tyrosine. Subsequent substitutions provided incremental KM improvements with minor kcat effects, 'tuning' the system. Expression levels remained consistent across all intermediates.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C49 describe the kinetic effects of successive substitutions. The S41Y kinetic data (C45) is shown in Figure 4B-G, the mechanistic interpretation (C46-C47) is supported by prior work (Copp et al., 2017) and structural reasoning, the tuning effect (C48) is evident in Figure 4C-F, and consistent expression (C49) is confirmed by SDS-PAGE in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

results.result: Error-prone PCR mutagenesis across the entire nfsA gene yielded 50 unique chloramphenicol-resistant variants, all containing R225 substitutions (100%), while 20 unselected clones had no R225 mutations. Codon 225 was mutated exclusively at the first nucleotide position (R225C, R225S, or R225G), providing compelling evidence that R225 substitution is the most attainable way to eliminate quinone competition as a key first step in evolving chloramphenicol detoxification.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C55 present independent validation through epPCR. The sequencing data (C50-C52) from Supplementary files 1e-f show 100% R225 substitution in selected variants (C53) versus 0% in unselected controls (C51), strongly supporting the conclusions about the importance of R225 elimination (C54-C55). The specific nucleotide position bias (C52) is an interesting observation though the mechanistic explanation is speculative.

results.result: Testing against five structurally diverse prodrugs showed that four had largely unchanged activity (0.8-2-fold) with the evolved variants, while metronidazole showed similar gains to chloramphenicol despite structural dissimilarity. R225V/D substitutions only significantly enhanced activity with metronidazole and CB1954, indicating selection was not driven exclusively by loss of quinone competition.
results.evaluation: Claims C56-C59 present prodrug specificity data from Figure 5. The lack of generic enhancement across all prodrugs (C56) and specific gains with metronidazole (C57) are clearly shown. The selective enhancement by R225 substitutions (C58) and the inference about mechanism (C59) are well-supported, demonstrating that substrate-specific effects beyond simple quinone competition contributed to the selection outcome.

results.result: The evolved variants showed dual selectable/counter-selectable properties: chloramphenicol maintained plasmids bearing 36_37 or 20_39 in 100% of cases (94/94), while metronidazole forced plasmid elimination in 100% of cases (94/94), suggesting potential applications as dual-purpose marker genes.
results.evaluation: Claims C60-C63 describe a practical application. The properties of metronidazole (C60) are supported by citation to Chan-Hyams et al., 2018. The experimental validation (C61-C62) shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1 demonstrates perfect selection/counter-selection (100% success rate), though the sample size is modest. The suggested application (C63) is appropriately presented as speculative.

results.result: The strong trade-off between quinone and chloramphenicol reduction differs from predominantly weak trade-offs in previous laboratory evolution studies. The findings support the proposal that natural evolution involves both positive selection for new functions and negative selection against original functions, with positive selection alone insufficient for specialization. Evolution in the natural intracellular milieu involves both types of selection.
results.evaluation: Claims C67-C73 place the findings in broader evolutionary context. The comparison to previous studies (C67-C69) is supported by appropriate citations. The interpretation about selection pressures (C70-C73) is well-supported by the data showing complete loss of quinone activity, retention of most promiscuous activities, and the specific enhancement of chloramphenicol reduction, consistent with the cited theoretical framework from Kaltenbach et al., 2016.

results.result: NfsA is less essential than ProA to host fitness, allowing evolution without gene duplication when promiscuous functions become essential. Only a minority of enzymes are under active selection at any time, and metabolic redundancy provides latent evolutionary potential. A single mutation eliminating native substrate competition can rapidly amplify promiscuous activity, conferring cellular robustness even if individual enzymes are less robust.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C81 discuss broader evolutionary implications. The comparison to ProA (C74-C75) is supported by citation to Ackerley et al., 2004. The evolutionary interpretation (C76, C78-C81) is well-supported by the data and appropriately contextualized with citations to Bergthorsson et al., 2007 and Newton et al., 2015. The inference about cellular robustness (C80-C81) is reasonable given the demonstrated rapid functional shift via single R225 substitution.

results.result: The approach of focusing on eight active-site residues means the reconstructed NfsA 'engine' is unlikely optimal within the pre-existing chassis, and further gains would result from selecting second-shell substitutions. However, this approach avoids the limitations of error-prone PCR, which can only access 5.7 of 19 alternative amino acids per position on average with bias toward similar residues.
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C66 acknowledge methodological limitations and advantages. The acknowledgment of suboptimality (C64-C65) is appropriately speculative and reasonable. The limitation of epPCR (C66) is supported by citation to Hermes et al., 1990 and provides valid justification for the chosen approach, though the trade-offs between methods could be more thoroughly discussed.

results.result: Previous laboratory evolution studies typically showed weak activity trade-offs and progression via generalist intermediates. Two competing hypotheses explain this: enzyme robustness/plasticity (Tawfik) versus experimental bias toward positive selection without negative selection (Tokuriki). Previous studies were also biased toward heterologous enzymes and exogenous substrates.
results.evaluation: Claims C87-C92 summarize prior theoretical frameworks through appropriate citations to Kaltenbach et al., 2016, Aharoni et al., 2005. These claims accurately represent the cited literature and establish the context for why the current study's findings (strong trade-offs, native enzyme, endogenous substrate competition) are significant and address gaps in previous work.
